name: RedTeam / Innerworks
title: "We're not afraid of hyper-intelligent bot swarms on the internet. We use them to optimise our technology." When we launched RedTeam almost two years ago we could clearly see where the internet was heading. We've since seen clients with over 90% of their traffic made up of not just automation but highly intelligent bot swarms, capable of bypassing any traditional detection mechanism. The only way to combat a threat like this is to welcome it and learn from it. By constantly ingesting and evolving attack vectors from a hive mind of miners, a Bittensor powered defence has now become the only reliable source of protection on the internet.

name: RedTeam / Innerworks
title: Every challenge we’ve run on the subnet is now archived at https://theredteam.io/challenges, with a walkthrough of what problems they're actually solving. Each challenge targets one way fraud hides online, from anti-detect browsers, extensions and automation frameworks to VPN traffic, spoofed devices and bots built to move like people. Running these in parallel covers more attack surface than any in-house security team could staff. Over the last 30 days miners committed 4,258 submissions, and the immune system multiplies that 2 to 3x by evolving each attack against our defences. All of it feeds the products our clients run in production. Everything we laid out on Novelty Search for the end of the year is progressing faster than we expected. We’re working to make as much of it public as we can, with more to follow as each deal and partnership closes. This week our CEO @oli_innerworks will be live on one of the largest broadcast networks, talking about RedTeam and why decentralised intelligence is where cybersecurity has to go.

title: The future of cybersecurity will be dictated by a defender's ability to not only ingest unique attacks, but generate the strains that don't exist yet and ship the detection ahead of them. As the rest of the industry degrades, the largest financial institutions will consolidate on the single provider that can do this at scale. That provider needs a constant supply of unique attacks to work from, and a subnet is the only structure that pays a swarm of attackers to supply them. bittensor:native #SN61
